title: Step 6 was a drag of the exhausted Petal Pixie from base toward a battlefield. The engine correctly offered no standardMove (unit is exhausted) so the drag was a no-op and state is unchanged — that part is correct. However the AFTER screenshot shows a toast "Move rejected: Move 'playUnit' condition not met". This is the late-arriving server rejection of step 5's 'Play Unit Soaring Scout to base' c
expected: Trace confirms sequence: step 4 snapshot (after clicking Play Petal Pixie) still shows energy 2 and both playUnit moves (stale, pre-move_accepted); step 5 clicked the still-rendered "Play Unit Soaring Scout to base" button; step 5 snapshot shows energy 0, no playUnit in moves; 06.png shows toast "Move rejected: Move 'playUnit' condition not met" (05.png has no toast). Drag in step 6 cannot emit playUnit (drag-drop.js:86-97 only matches standardMove for base), so the toast is step 5's rejection. Source: websocket.js:148 `showToast(`Move rejected: ${msg.error}`)` passes the raw engine string through verbatim; the string originates at packages/core/src/engine/rule-engine.ts:833 (`Move '${moveId}' condition not met`, emitted whenever a condition returns bare `false`), and playUnit's condition returns plain boolean from canAffordCard (play-unit.ts:451ff) with no ConditionFailure reason, so an unaffordable play can never produce a player-facing "not enough energy" message. Sidebar action buttons (render/actions.js:431-441) call executeMove directly from availableMoves with no in-flight guard, so a second click before move_accepted arrives sends a stale move. Server ws-game.ts:103-108 forwards error unchanged.
